name: Ariselu
subtitle: rice flour and jaggery discs fried for Sankranti, chewy and dark

ingredients.qty: 400g, soaked 4 hours then dried and ground
ingredients.note: the flour must be slightly damp, which is why it is ground at home

prepNotes: The jaggery syrup stage decides everything. Too soft and the discs dissolve in the oil; too hard and they are inedible.
Test it: a drop of syrup in cold water should form a ball you can roll between your fingers.

steps.text: Melt the jaggery with the water and boil to the soft-ball stage, about 8 minutes.
steps.tip: Drop a little into cold water. It should gather into a soft ball, not a thread and not a brittle sheet.

steps.text: Take off the heat and stir in the rice flour, sesame and cardamom quickly, while the syrup is still hot.
Knead into a soft dough while just cool enough to handle. Rest it 4 hours or overnight.
steps.tip: The rest lets the flour drink the syrup. Skipping it gives a hard ariselu.

steps.text: Pat portions into 8cm discs between two greased sheets of plastic.
Fry one at a time on medium, spooning oil over the top, until deep brown, about 3 minutes.
steps.tip: One at a time. They are fragile and stick to each other.

steps.text: Press each one between two flat spoons as it comes out to squeeze the oil back.

storage: Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight tin at room temperature and firms up over the first few days, which is normal.
